title: Reso Bass — approximate factory recreation
method: Source-only FFT and waveform inspection of the opening phrase. The sustained opening family is 36.7/73.5/110/146.7 Hz (D1); the high stabs are 73.4 Hz D2 and 65.4 Hz C2. The middle run resolves to F1, G1, F1, E1, F1, E1 by multiple harmonic spacings. Attack restarts and near-silent gaps determine the gate estimates. No Septum audio was used to choose note pitches.
uncertainties: ESTIMATED MIDI: original performance MIDI is unavailable. Notes, onsets, note-offs and overlaps are interpretations of the source MP3, not recovered original events.
Velocity 100 is an explicit constant placeholder, not an estimate of the original key velocities. Note-off velocity is 64. No original controller or pedal events have been recovered.
The factory parameter dump is unavailable. The companion patch is a newly authored approximate recreation, not exact factory SysEx; an exported SysEx file encodes this approximation only.

Audio frequencies do not uniquely reveal played key numbers: original oscillator tuning, octave switches and system transpose are unknown. The MIDI and companion patch jointly choose an octave interpretation.

Times are measured from decoded source MP3 audio; encoder delay, hardware response latency and prior effect state are not removed. Timing is approximate, generally 20–40 ms; short transitions can be less certain.
The brief middle run is less certain than the separated first four notes. Pitch bend or glide during attacks is simplified to discrete key changes.
The source has time-varying timbre and level; the static patch approximates the opening envelope without recovering live knob movement.

patch_design.name: APX ResoBass
rationale: A single saw family, resonant 24 dB low-pass and falling filter envelope reproduce the opening bright attack becoming a dark held bass.
The sustained reference eventually emphasizes roughly 147–183 Hz; the approximate cutoff and envelope target that range in Septum.
Effects are disabled because the chosen excerpt has nearly silent gaps and little evidence of a long reverb tail.

Preview spectrum showed the original draft envelope opening beyond the audible band for too long. Reduced depth and decay put its resonance sweep closer to the visible opening descent; this remains an approximate voicing change, not a recovered hardware parameter.
uncertainties: All voicing values are authored approximation parameters, not measured or recovered Roland factory parameter values.
The brief middle run is less certain than the separated first four notes. Pitch bend or glide during attacks is simplified to discrete key changes.
The source has time-varying timbre and level; the static patch approximates the opening envelope without recovering live knob movement.
